subject: Combining Upfront Voucher with Prepaid Discount — EcoHub Labs
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam@ecohub.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Promo voucher + Prepaid discount question

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — EcoHub is excited about the latency profile on image-to-text pipelines. A quick procurement question: our accelerator coordinator confirmed a $15k onboarding voucher (promo) and we're also evaluating a 6-month prepaid commit that would qualify for a standard 10% committed discount.

Procurement is asking whether we can apply the onboarding voucher against the prepaid committed invoice (effectively stacking the voucher and the prepaid discount) or if you treat the voucher as a post-invoice credit.

Can you confirm how Redwood usually handles this for accelerator cohorts? If needed, we can share a fast SOW and projected consumption.

Cheers,
Sam Rivera
Head of Platform Partnerships — EcoHub Labs
attachments: EcoHub_SOW_draft.pdf (attached)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Rivera <sam@ecohub.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promo voucher + Prepaid discount question

Hi Sam — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answer: we can support combining a voucher with a prepaid commit, but there are two operational paths and one legal nuance to watch for.

Options (high level):
- Apply voucher as an upfront credit that reduces the first invoice amount (voucher offsets prepaid invoice).
- Apply voucher as a post-invoice rebate/credit after usage; preserves accounting separation for certain finance flows.

Key nuance: if EcoHub wants the voucher to reduce the committed billing obligation (i.e., counts toward the commit), Legal needs to confirm language in the promo terms so it doesn’t create duplicate discounts against revenue recognition. That’s why we copied Ben (sales) and Lauren (finance/commercial).

If you can share expected start date and monthly consumption estimate we’ll draft the SOW/pricing table and run the legal checkbox.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Promo voucher + Prepaid discount question

Neha, Lauren — marking for quick sync. My take: we prefer to apply the voucher as an upfront credit against the first prepaid invoice for accelerator customers when possible — it simplifies billing and reporting for both parties.

Pros:
- Customer sees lower initial cash outflow (helpful for cohort conversions).
- Easier to reconcile in billing system (single invoice with credit applied).

Cons / caveat:
- Finance may want the voucher to be separately tracked for revenue recognition if the voucher was granted as a marketing/promo expense versus a commercial discount.

I can draft the pricing_matrix.xlsx showing both flows. Lauren, can you advise on any rev-rec guardrails that would block applying the voucher against the committed billing?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head, Partnerships & Programs

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Promo voucher + Prepaid discount question

Ben / Neha — quick note from finance/commercial: we can accept the voucher as an upfront credit applied to the first prepaid invoice under two conditions:

1) The promo voucher must be documented in the SOW (line item: Promo Voucher — $15,000) and flagged as a contra-revenue marketing allowance in our ledger.
2) The prepaid commit discount (10%) should be calculated on the net amount after voucher application, OR we can calculate the discount on the gross committed amount and then apply the voucher as a separate contra line. Both are possible but have different accounting treatments — EcoHub should confirm preferred presentation.

If EcoHub wants the committed discount to apply on gross (and then voucher subtracted) we must ensure the SOW/contract reflects that to avoid restatement risk.

I’ve put a recommended illustration into pricing_matrix.xlsx (attached). If legal needs to add language about promo stacking we’ll coordinate.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_matrix.xlsx (internal)

Subject: Re: Promo voucher + Prepaid discount question

Thanks everyone — that all makes sense. EcoHub prefers seeing the 10% committed discount calculated on the gross prepaid amount, then the $15k voucher applied as a contra line on the first invoice (presentation B in your spreadsheet). Procurement confirmed that flow keeps their internal budget intact.

Next steps for us:
- I’ll upload a signed SOW with the voucher line and the presentation preference to DocuSign today.
- Can Redwood confirm you’ll apply the voucher to the first prepaid invoice once the DocuSign completes?

If yes, we’re good to proceed and I’ll loop our finance lead for payment scheduling.

Best,
Sam Rivera
Head of Platform Partnerships — EcoHub Labs
